questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To utilise and my language skills, to come closer to the alps but also information from others

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I truly emnjoyed my stay there, I had indeed a wonderful time. However, German beuraucracy, lack of digitlisation, poor housing situation as well as the administrative procedure at KU brings down the average experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was allocated a German buddy who helped me with everything from local guidance to logistics and administrative errands. A very good experience

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Don't know, did not look into it mych as I got it allocated

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Shared kitchen in shared flats. A campus cantine with affordabe prices

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for poor cleaning routines and poor administrative staff

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The application process was simple and it was easy to get accommadated. However, the operational and administrative work was porr

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have a "shopping week" before you decide what courses you want to take, so that you can get a sense of the courses before you register. So the course catalogue is hypothetical until they know how many people actually register.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online guides, in-person assistance and more

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Fully

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much about it, it will be resolved on the spot

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Reallly appreciated the smalle class groups and the more interactive style of teaching, with focus on presentations, discussions and active participation

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Think they were at the right level. Just the right amount of difficulty and challenging and developing in other ways than at KU

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Smaller groups, more interactive, more active participation, more presentations and more discussions

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
JUR-16170 International law in practice
SLI-21100 GO-Konstanz German intensive A2.1
INT-10770 Regional policy in the European Union: Policies, institutions and public 
INT-10830 Terrorism and Law
POL-31590 The political consequences of technological change 
POL-31610 Workplace ties: The role of social relationships in organizations

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them were really fun. However POL-31590 The political consequences of technological change had a more narrow focus than expected. And JUR-16170 International law in practice can be tricky if you're not comfy with oral exams

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Really like the sports-ticket, the cultural ticket and all the activities going on around the lake and the alps

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Opera, theatre, orchestra, karaoke, skiing, snowshoe-hiking, normal hiking, trips to surrounding places in the alps

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Karaoke, cultural ticket and sport facilities were great fun! And get around and explore the alps and the lake! Take a biketrip around the lake! Get a Deutschland-ticket and travel around in Germany. And use the Interrail-pass provided by Erasmus sustainable travel

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take a trip around the lake! Or rent a car and drive to Liechtenstein!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Think the poor digitisation and the lack of wifi and card payment was the hardest part.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Sign up for the buddy-programme.
Get involved in local sports clubs, choirs or workplaces

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The lack of digital services.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Christmas markets, carnival, other outdoor activites. And overall more chill with alcohol

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Sign up for the buddy programme!
Participate in GO Konstanz!
Be ready to bring cash and to print a lot of stuff

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing that I can come up with

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the people I met and all the places I've seen

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My flatmates

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Have fun!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
